cells.title: Response to PB8C
cells.reviewerComment:
Weaknesses:
1. Updating the Gaussian covariance with the Jacobian of a deformation field is the core idea of PhysGaussian (Xie et al., CVPR 2024), which is not cited.

2. Missing related works. CAP4D and GAF also build head avatars from generated multi-view data. They should be discussed. VASA-3D appeared in December 2025, so it is not really concurrent and needs more discussion.

3. The method is trained per subject and per audio clip (about 6 hours each), and is tested on the same audio it was fitted to. The baselines are animatable avatars that must generalize to new driving signals. Also, how are the baselines driven at test time? For example, GA is “trained on real multi-view scan videos”, so where do its FLAME parameters for the test audio come from?

Specific Points of Feedback for Rebuttal:
1. What is the difference between IDR and the covariance update in PhysGaussian?
2. How are the baselines driven at test time, and what data were GA and HR trained on?
3. Which view latent is used at inference when the frontal view is held out?
cells.content:
Q1 (W1). The covariance update is the same as PhysGaussian's ($\Sigma'=J\Sigma J^T$, first-order kinematics); we will cite it. The difference is where J comes from and what it is for. In PhysGaussian, motion is given, not learned: J is accumulated by forward MPM simulation with prescribed materials. In IDR, motion is unknown and learned from inconsistent videos (an inverse problem): J is the Jacobian of a field $x+MLP(x,t,v)$ fit to the videos. Their purposes also differ: PhysGaussian uses the update to render simulated motion consistently; we use it to remove rotation and scale as free per-Gaussian parameters so that view contradictions cannot be absorbed by distorting single Gaussians (Fig. 6c).
// J differentiates a field learned from inconsistent videos, and in stages 1-6 rotation/scale have no free parameters, so view contradictions cannot be absorbed by distorting single Gaussians (Fig. 6, G). 
Q2 (W3). All baselines but ARTalk get the same performance: the HeyGen frontal video of the test audio. GA: driven by FLAME tracked from HeyGen frontal videos. HR: trained on the 15 HeyGen views, driven by its encoder. GAG/LAM: one-shot, tracked FLAME. ARTalk: audio to FLAME. 4DGS/HR share our per-audio regime. We will group baselines by regime and state that ours cannot re-animate. Real-data novel views: <E1>; side views: <E2>. 
Q3. Cam 191, the training camera closest to the head's forward axis (<E6>); cam 037 is held out. W2. We will discuss CAP4D, GAF and VASA-3D: all are FLAME-bound; CAP4D/GAF generate consistent views with their own diffusion models, VASA-3D uses VASA-1 latents. Ours is template-free and uses only output videos of any 2D generator.

cells.title: Response to YQJy
cells.reviewerComment:
Weaknesses:

1. The method is not fully audio-driven in the usual sense. During training, the model uses learnable features indexed by time and is optimized for a particular subject and audio sequence. At inference, there is no audio encoder that maps a new speech signal to the corresponding motion. The method therefore seems closer to audio-specific 4D reconstruction than to a reusable audio-to-3D animation model.
2. The evaluation is closely tied to HeyGen. HeyGen is used to generate both the training videos and the pseudo-reference videos used in evaluation. This makes it difficult to determine whether the method recovers realistic facial motion or mainly reproduces the artifacts and biases of the teacher model. Results on real multi-view speaking videos or genuinely unseen audio would make the claims much stronger.
3. Some important details and comparisons are missing. Several recent methods are omitted because their code is unavailable, so the “state-of-the-art” claim should be stated more cautiously. The paper also calls the proposed component an “implicit differential regularizer,” but the stated objective contains only L1 and SSIM terms. It is unclear whether there is an additional regularization loss or whether the regularization effect comes entirely from the parameterization. The user study would also benefit from confidence intervals and significance testing.

Specific Points of Feedback for Rebuttal:

1. Clarify the task definition and generalization capability. Please specify whether the model can animate the same subject using unseen audio without generating new pseudo-videos or performing subject-specific re-optimization. If this is not possible, the claims regarding “audio-driven” 3D generation should be revised. Experiments on unseen audio would be essential.
2. Strengthen the evaluation protocol and address pseudo-ground-truth bias. Please report results on real multi-view talking-head videos, clarify the camera and data split, and confirm that held-out views are not used during initialization or fine-tuning. Per-subject statistics, confidence intervals, significance tests, and a more rigorously documented user study should also be provided.**
cells.content:
Task. Correct: new audio requires new pseudo-videos and re-optimization (2-6 h, Supp. Tab. 4; Sec. 6), so unseen audio cannot be animated directly. We will revise "audio-driven" wording to audio-specific 4D talking-head generation. Generality comes from the 2D model: any speaker, style or language it handles can be lifted without multi-view speech data. 

HeyGen bias. Only the Tab. 3 ablation uses HeyGen frames as reference. LSE-D/C score renders against the input audio, CPBD is no-reference, CSIM is vs. the real neutral image of held-out cam 037. Motion is bounded by the 2D teacher as an upper-bound reference. Gains persist with open-source LTX-2 (Supp. Tab. 5, moved to main paper). Real synchronized NeRSemble speech vs. held-out real footage: <E1>  

Split. Cam 037 is never used for canonical GS, open-mouth fine-tuning or training; inference uses training cam 191's latent. 

Statistics. User study: ours is preferred over all 6 baselines on all 3 criteria (180 judgments each; binomial p_Holm<1e-8); weakest is GAGAvatar lip sync, 71.7% [63.6, 79.6] (95% CI); ours wins for all 9 subjects. Metrics vs. 4DGS: <E5>. Full protocol will be added.

Wording. "State-of-the-art" will be limited to open baselines. IDR adds no loss term (Implicit); its effect is the parameterization.

cells.title: Response to Bjx3
cells.reviewerComment:
Weaknesses:

1. HeyGen is a closed, quota-limited commercial service, which hinders reproducibility and makes results sensitive to model version drift. The open-source LTX-2 results (Supp. Table 5) show substantially worse performance for all methods (LSE-D 8.94 vs 7.87), indicating that output quality is strongly coupled to the 2D model; this evidence should be surfaced in the main paper.
2. Re-animating with new audio requires retraining (pseudo videos are generated per audio), precluding real-time use. Reduced-iteration variants (2–3h, Supp. Table 4) mitigate but do not remove the limitation; the efficiency trade-off against one-shot baselines deserves a clearer scope statement.
3. Canonical locations/scales/rotations are fixed during deformation training (no densification), so the mouth interior depends on the ad-hoc "open-mouth fine-tuning" step whose frame-selection criteria are under-specified; alpha/color are shared across time and views, limiting intra-mouth appearance dynamics (teeth/tongue) and per-view illumination differences; the first-order Jacobian approximation (Eq. 5) is accurate only for small Gaussians/small deformations, and the extent to which the residual MLPs compensate for large-motion errors is not analyzed.
4. Training is view-conditioned but inference uses only the near-frontal camera's latent (Supp. Sec. B); the selection rule and whether this biases head pose/expressiveness at extreme views are not examined (e.g., a sensitivity experiment swapping the inference view latent).
5. Missing related work and comparisons. (a) SyncTrack4D [^1] addresses the same core challenge (multi-view inconsistency) via explicit cross-video track alignment and synchronization before 4DGS fitting—a complementary "align-then-fuse" strategy that should be discussed or partially compared; (b) uncertainty-aware regularization for 4DGS under weak supervision (UA-4DGS [^2]) is a complementary stabilization strategy to IDR; (c) the template-free vs template-bound trade-off versus VASA-3D (FLAME + residuals, single image) is only briefly stated. These are discussable/clarifiable rather than fatal.

[^1]: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.04315v1 — SyncTrack4D: Cross-Video Motion Alignment and Video Synchronization for Multi-Video 4D Gaussian Splatting [^2]: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.08879v1 — UA-4DGS: 4D Gaussian Splatting in the Wild with Uncertainty-Aware Regularization (NeurIPS 2024)

Specific Points of Feedback for Rebuttal:

1. Can you provide results on genuinely synchronized multi-view talking sequences (e.g., real NeRSemble videos) for your method and the reconstruction baselines, to show the method does not sacrifice performance in favorable conditions? Relatedly, can you report GA on its native real multi-view data as an anchor for how much the pseudo-data regime hurts consistency-based baselines?
2. Please provide quantitative side-view metrics (e.g., LSE-C/CSIM on 2–3 non-frontal cameras) to substantiate the novel-view coherence claim beyond qualitative figures and the user study.
3. How is the "most frontal" inference view latent selected, and how sensitive are the results to this choice? Does fixing the frontal view latent systematically bias head motion or reduce expressiveness at extreme view angles?
4. Could you move the LTX-2 (open-source generator) results into the main paper and state explicitly how much of the final quality is bounded by the 2D generator's fidelity?
5. In Table 3, removing IDR improves PSNR (34.315 vs 34.095). Please explain what IDR trades off on the PSNR axis and provide localized quantitative evidence (e.g., masked mouth/teeth region SSIM/LPIPS) for its structural benefit.
6. Please detail the "open-mouth fine-tuning" frame-selection criteria, its sensitivity across subjects, and its failure modes (e.g., if the 2D model rarely opens the mouth, as with LTX-2).
7. Could you discuss (and ideally partially evaluate) whether explicit cross-view alignment (e.g., SyncTrack4D-style dense track matching) before 4DGS fitting would complement or replace your implicit view-conditioned fusion? Also discuss how IDR relates to uncertainty-aware and rigidity regularizers for weakly supervised 4DGS.**
cells.content:
1. Related work comparison
(1) Template-free main motion (vs. SurFhead and TeGA). In both methods, the main motion comes from a tracked template mesh. SurFhead binds Gaussians to FLAME triangles and derives its Jacobian from their deformation, 
J=EE-1. TeGA maps Gaussians through a tracked 3DMM mesh and uses J=JF+JD, where the mesh term JF carries the coarse motion and JD, derived from a learned residual deformation field as in our method, only refines fine details the mesh misses; it also requires an explicit Frobenius-norm penalty to remain stable. In our method, a learned deformation field carries the entire motion without any template, which our setting requires, as tracking is unreliable on independently generated views and fails on stylized characters, and we use its Jacobian as a regularizer under inconsistent supervision rather than as a refinement of tracked motion. 
(2) Hierarchical encoding vs. E-D3DGS. The key difference is that E-D3DGS models time only, whereas we also model per-view deviations at each moment. E-D3DGS uses a multi-scale temporal representation with two separate decoders for coarse and fine motion, whose outputs are added; at a given moment, all views share one deformation, so it cannot reconcile views that disagree at that moment. We instead use a single network and place the hierarchy in the latent space: latents at multiple temporal resolutions (T, T/2, T/4, …) are summed into one input embedding. This is done for two latents: a shared time latent t(t), capturing motion common to all views, and a per-view latent v(t), capturing how each view deviates at each moment (Eq. 10). 

2. Real data, 5 training (our HeyGen IV/LTX-2 cameras), 11 held-out views: <E1>

3. Frontal latent across azimuths vs. baselines: <E2>. Latent sensitivity: <E3>. Minor. <E5>; Tab. 1 lip-sync margins over 4DGS are not significant, so we will claim matching the teacher. We will add a unified cost table.


// Condense old:
// We will cite and reposition: Jacobian covariance transport (TeGA, SurFhead) and multi-scale time codes (E-D3DGS). SurFhead uses deformation gradients of tracked FLAME triangles; TeGA differentiates a residual field on a tracked 3DMM, in UVD space, from consistent real captures, with a Jacobian-norm penalty. Ours is template-free and uses a world-space field under contradictory supervision: in stages 1-6 rotation/scale have no free parameters, so conflicts cannot be absorbed per Gaussian; gains peak where views disagree most (inner mouth, high inconsistency: SSIM 0.420→0.520). E-D3DGS models time only, assuming consistent views; we add time-indexed per-view latents φv(t) to a shared φt, separating motion from view-specific deviations. Our main contribution is lifting contradictory 2D talking videos into one template-free 4DGS.

cells.title: Response to tvP1
cells.reviewerComment:
Weaknesses:

- The novelty seems incremental. The IDR's idea of propagating deformation to Gaussian rotation and scale via the Jacobian is closely similar to what is proposed in TeGA [a] and SurFhead [b]. For the hierarchical time- and view-dependent deformation, the idea of multi-scale temporal representation has already been adopted in related dynamic Gaussian splatting work: E-D3DGS [c] uses coarse and fine temporal embeddings for deformable 3DGS.

- All evaluation is circular; no result is validated against real data. Every metric in the paper uses HeyGen output as reference (the Table 1 "upper bound" and the ablation proxy-GT alike).

- Inference is anchored to one view latent (the near-frontal camera, Sec. 4.7) with no sensitivity analysis, and whether the shared representation consolidates geometry across views is never measured.

- Minor:

1. Sec. E reports the method's own costs but no unified comparison of training time, inference latency, and memory across baselines.
2. Table 1's lip-sync margins over 4DGS are very small and are reported without variance or significance testing.
3. A number-of-views ablation is missing.

References: [a] Li et al., "TeGA: Texture Space Gaussian Avatars for High-Resolution Dynamic Head Modeling," SIGGRAPH 2025.

[b] Lee et al., "SurFhead: Affine Rig Blending for Geometrically Accurate 2D Gaussian Surfel Head Avatars," ICLR 2025.

[c] Bae et al., "Per-Gaussian Embedding-Based Deformation for Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting," ECCV 2024.

Specific Points of Feedback for Rebuttal:

1. Please discuss the novelty of the IDR and the hierarchical time- and view-dependent deformation relative to the papers cited above.

2. Can you evaluate the reconstruction pipeline on real data? For example, train on 15 views of a real NeRSemble dynamic sequence and report PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS on the held-out view against the real footage. Although this does not test the handling of inconsistency, it would validate that the proposed components faithfully reconstruct 4D content from real multi-view video, which no current result establishes.

3. Can you provide quantitative results beyond the near-frontal view at inference? For example, report performance using several azimuths. If the method resolves cross-view inconsistency as claimed, its quality should degrade less from frontal to side views than the baselines, which the current near-frontal-only evaluation cannot show.**
cells.content:
Q1. No. Held-out cam 037 is never used for canonical GS, open-mouth fine-tuning or training; inference uses training cam 191's latent. 

Q2. Existing: Tab. 1 LSE/CPBD are on held-out cam 037, while CSIM is computed on front-to-side sweep renders vs. real subject neutral image; side views were otherwise assessed only in the user study. We had no depth/geometry measurements and acknowledge this gap. New: real NeRSemble speech vs. 11 held-out real views: <E1>. Side views vs. baselines: <E2> 

Q3. All tables use hand-picked HeyGen open-mouth frames from training views; only Fig. 6c uses a real teeth capture. 

Q4. IDR's frame-level Tab. 3 gains are small; we will say so. Without IDR, free rotation/scale fit view-specific detail and smooth the mouth, which PSNR rewards under misalignment. Locally IDR helps: mouth-mask LPIPS 0.261→0.255 (8/9 subjects, p=0.045); high-inconsistency inner-mouth SSIM 0.420→0.520. The user study used the sharpened model; sharpening inflates CPBD, so Tab. 1 also reports the unsharpened model, already above 4DGS/HR in CPBD and CSIM. 

Setting. We will state inputs (15 views, one 2D generator, ~6 h per subject-audio) and group baselines by input regime.

cells.title: Response to 6F2T
cells.reviewerComment:
Weaknesses:

- The central claim is coherent 4D reconstruction, but the paper does not directly measure 3D geometry or cross-view consistency. LSE, CPBD, CSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, and SSIM are 2D metrics and cannot establish that the learned view-conditioned deformation corresponds to a shared dynamic geometry.
- The model is trained on HeyGen-generated pseudo videos and is also evaluated against HeyGen frames as proxy ground truth. This circularity primarily measures how well the method reproduces the chosen 2D generator, not whether it recovers real multi-view facial motion.
- The practical setting is more restrictive than the term “audio-driven 3D talking head” may suggest: it uses 16 input views, invokes a 2D video generator for each view, and requires approximately six hours of subject- and audio-specific optimization. A new audio clip requires re-optimization.
- The baseline table mixes person-specific optimization methods, one-shot avatar models, and adapted methods with different inputs and training data. Several highly relevant recent methods are absent because code is unavailable.
- The optional sharpening stage substantially increases CPBD while reducing PSNR, LPIPS, and SSIM, illustrating that the main sharpness metric can reward post-processing rather than more accurate reconstruction.

Specific Points of Feedback for Rebuttal:

1. Please precisely state whether any held-out evaluation camera contributes to canonical reconstruction or initialization.
2. Please provide any existing cross-view consistency, held-out-camera, depth, or geometry measurements that are not visible in the main paper.
3. Please distinguish all experiments that use real open-mouth captures from those using only generated pseudo frames.
4. Please correct or explain the IDR ablation interpretation and identify which model variant was shown in the user study.**
cells.content:
Q1. No. Held-out cam 037 is never used for canonical GS, open-mouth fine-tuning or training; inference uses training cam 191's latent. 

Q2. Existing: Tab. 1 LSE/CPBD are on held-out cam 037, while CSIM is computed on front-to-side sweep renders vs. real subject neutral image; side views were otherwise assessed only in the user study. We had no depth/geometry measurements and acknowledge this gap. New: real NeRSemble speech vs. 11 held-out real views: <E1>. Side views vs. baselines: <E2> 

Q3. All tables use hand-picked HeyGen open-mouth frames from training views; only Fig. 6c uses a real teeth capture. 

Q4. IDR's frame-level Tab. 3 gains are small; we will say so. Without IDR, free rotation/scale fit view-specific detail and smooth the mouth, which PSNR rewards under misalignment. Locally IDR helps: mouth-mask LPIPS 0.261→0.255 (8/9 subjects, p=0.045); high-inconsistency inner-mouth SSIM 0.420→0.520. The user study used the sharpened model; sharpening inflates CPBD, so Tab. 1 also reports the unsharpened model, already above 4DGS/HR in CPBD and CSIM. 

Setting. We will state inputs (15 views, one 2D generator, ~6 h per subject-audio) and group baselines by input regime.

cells.title: Response to AI
cells.reviewerComment:
Weaknesses

- Cross-view coherence is not established by the formulation or evaluation. Equations (2), (7), and (8) condition every geometric transform on view, Equation (11) contains no cross-view agreement term, and Section 4.7 selects only the frontal latent at inference; the model therefore permits different deformation fields for different training views. Because Section 5 evaluates a held-out frontal view and Table 2 reports preference rather than geometric consistency or reference-based side-view fidelity, the central claim requires held-out multi-camera evaluation and frontal-only or independent-view controls.
- The introduction’s claim of “superior lip-sync quality” and preservation of “more high-frequency detail than six” baselines is not supported by any single Table 1 row. The full model’s LSE-D is 7.908 versus 4DGS’s better 7.890, and its CPBD is 0.441 versus GAGAvatar’s better 0.444; without sharpening, CPBD falls to 0.343 and trails four baselines. The best positive LSE-D margin is only 0.022 against a total table spread of 2.510, with no variance estimates or real-video calibration, so the evidence supports competitive overall performance rather than categorical objective superiority.
- The novelty positioning omits closely related published work. Portrait4D-v2 already learns a 4D head synthesizer from pseudo-multiview videos, while AniGS explicitly formulates reconstruction from inconsistent generated views as a 4D Gaussian problem; neither appears in the target paper’s references or tables (Deng et al., 2024; Qiu et al., 2025). MGGTalk is also an uncited audio-driven Gaussian talking-head method supporting novel viewpoints, contradicting the statement that EmoTalk3D and GaussianSpeech are the “only exceptions” sharing this goal (Gong et al., 2025).
- The claimed implicit differential regularization is neither structurally maintained nor strongly supported by Table 3. Equations (7)–(8) add unconstrained residual rotation and scale networks, and Section 4.2 explicitly states that no constraint keeps these residuals near identity; relative to the no-IDR row, the complete unsharpened model improves LPIPS, SSIM, and CSIM by only 0.001 each while worsening PSNR and CPBD. Without uncertainty estimates or measured failure rates, the qualitative examples do not establish a reliable contribution from this central component.

Suggestions for Improvement

- The paper would benefit from an early task-definition box separating capture, optimization, and playback. Sections 4.7 and 6 reveal that each subject-audio pair requires a newly optimized temporal sequence rather than producing a reusable audio-driven avatar, a distinction that should be explicit in the abstract and introduction.
- The role of the view variable should be explained with a schematic distinguishing the training-view identity from the camera used to render the final frontal-conditioned geometry. This would clarify what “frontal anchor,” “view-dependent deformation,” and “novel viewpoint” mean at each stage without requiring readers to reconcile Sections 4.1, 4.3, and 4.7.
- A systematic analysis over measured input inconsistency would better characterize the method’s operating regime. The current high-versus-low inconsistency distinction in Figure 6 is qualitative; stratification by cross-view pose, landmark, expression, or gaze disagreement would show when view conditioning helps and when reconstruction breaks down.
- Practical comparisons should separate capture efficiency from computation and reuse. Section 5 reports six hours of subject- and audio-specific optimization, so reporting capture cost, optimization cost, rendering cost, and re-animation capability separately would make the tradeoff against feed-forward and reusable avatar systems clearer.

Additional Details and Minor Issues

- In Equation (6), SVD guarantees rather than ; a determinant correction is needed if is used as a rotation.
- Equation (10) calls the latent combination a “normalized sum,” but no normalization is defined.
- Equation (8) permits nonpositive scales unless an activation or clamp is used.
- Section 4.5 describes a triplane using a resolution; plane dimensions and feature channels should be distinguished.
- Table 1 calls HeyGen an upper bound, although the reported no-reference metrics can exceed the source score.
- The abstract, Section 4, and Section 5 should consistently distinguish capture sessions, the 16 camera images, and the optional real open-mouth capture.**
cells.content:
Coherence. View latents differ only in training; at inference one Gaussian set per frame (frontal latent) is rendered from all cameras. Held-out multi-camera evaluation on real data: <E1>; side views: <E2>. 

Claims. Agreed: no single Tab. 1 row supports categorical superiority. We will state lip-sync matching the teacher, best CSIM and user preference, and call HeyGen a teacher reference, not an upper bound. 

Related work. We will cite Portrait4D-v2, AniGS and MGGTalk and drop "only exceptions". Portrait4D-v2's pseudo views come from a 3D-aware lifter and are consistent by construction; AniGS treats views of a static target as time, while we separate shared motion φt from time-varying per-view deviations φv(t). 

IDR. Residual MLPs are identity-initialized and train only in the final stage. Its effect is local: mouth-mask LPIPS 0.261→0.255 (8/9 subjects, p=0.045); under high inconsistency, inner-mouth SSIM 0.420→0.520. 

Suggestions. We will add a task box (capture, optimization, playback), a schematic separating training-view latent from render camera, and separate cost reporting. Fixes. det(U)=+1 by flipping a column (covariance unchanged); define Eq. 10's normalization; state how Eq. 8 keeps scales positive; separate triplane resolution from channels; distinguish captures consistently.
